sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and the 'Pulmonary Mask' Phenomenon
sections.description: This section introduces the clinical scenario of a pediatric patient presenting with recurrent respiratory distress, emphasizing the deceptive nature of Pancreatopleural Fistula (PPF). It details the initial physical examination findings, the progression of symptoms across multiple admissions, and the critical importance of recognizing when thoracic symptoms originate from abdominal pathology.
subtopics: Initial presentation: Recurrent right-sided pleural effusion, chest pain, and respiratory distress in a late-childhood male
Physical examination findings: Signs of large pleural effusion (stony dullness, reduced breath sounds) vs. absence of primary pulmonary signs
The 'Pulmonary Mask': How pancreatic pathology mimics primary thoracic diseases like tuberculosis or pneumonia
The diagnostic delay: Impact of incomplete history taking (concealed trauma) on initial management decisions
Red flags in recurrent effusions: Why repeated thoracocentesis without resolution warrants re-evaluation

sections.description: This section bridges the gap between the traumatic event and the final diagnosis. It explains the anatomical mechanisms allowing pancreatic fluid to reach the pleural space and outlines the step-by-step diagnostic algorithm used to differentiate PPF from other causes of hemorrhagic or amylase-rich pleural effusions.
subtopics: Anatomical pathway: Retroperitoneal tracking through the esophageal/aortic hiatus to the pleural cavity
Mechanism of injury: Blunt abdominal trauma causing pancreatic duct disruption and pseudocyst formation
Differential diagnosis strategy: Systematically ruling out TB (ADA/GeneXpert), malignancy, empyema, Boerhaave's syndrome, and hepatic/renal causes
Biochemical hallmarks: Interpretation of massively elevated pleural fluid amylase (>1000 IU/L) and lipase as pathognomonic for PPF
Imaging modalities: Role of CT in identifying retroperitoneal collections versus MRCP in defining ductal anatomy and fistula tracts

sections.section_title: Management Strategies: From Conservative to Interventional Approaches
sections.description: This section focuses on the therapeutic decision-making process for PPF in children. It contrasts conservative medical management with endoscopic and surgical options, detailing why specific treatments (bowel rest, octreotide) were chosen for this case and outlining the criteria for escalating care.
subtopics: Immediate stabilization: Respiratory support and drainage via intercostal catheter (ICD)
Conservative management protocol: Nil per oral (NPO), Total Parenteral Nutrition (TPN), and Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy (PERT)
Pharmacological adjuncts: Mechanism of action of Octreotide (somatostatin analogue) in reducing exocrine secretion
Step-wise escalation criteria: When to transition from medical management to ERCP/stenting or surgical intervention (distal pancreatectomy/Puestow)
Duration of therapy: Monitoring drainage output as a marker for fistula closure
